seoTitle: How to Move a Subtask to Another Task in Asana
metaDescription: Learn how to reassign a subtask to a different parent task in Asana in 2026 without losing comments, attachments, or collaborator history.
intro: Reorganizing project structure often means a subtask needs a new home, and Asana lets you re-parent it without recreating the work from scratch. This guide covers opening the task details panel, using the move option to change its parent, and confirming that history and collaborators transferred correctly.

steps.heading: Open the task details panel
steps.body: Open the parent task to locate the existing subtask you want to move.

steps.heading: Select the move option
steps.body: Select the subtask and choose the move icon to change its parent association.

steps.heading: Pick the new parent task
steps.body: Use the task picker to identify and select the new parent task the subtask should belong to.

steps.heading: Execute and verify the move
steps.body: Confirm the move action, then check that the subtask now appears under the new parent with its structure intact.

steps.heading: Review collaborators and dependencies
steps.body: Check that comments, collaborators, and any linked dependencies carried over correctly after re-parenting.

faq.question: Will comments and attachments stay with the subtask after moving it?
faq.answer: Yes, moving a subtask through the built-in move option preserves its comments, attachments, and metadata.

faq.question: Can I move a subtask to a task in a completely different project?
faq.answer: Yes, though you may need to check visibility settings if the target project has different privacy permissions than the original.

faq.question: Why can't I see a moved subtask on a private project board?
faq.answer: This usually happens when the subtask's new parent lives on a private project you don't have full visibility into, which can hide it from certain views.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for re-parenting subtasks?
faq.answer: Yes, Asana supports keyboard shortcuts for faster re-parenting across different project containers.
